correctness.rationale: Under symmetric cycle proposals the Metropolis edge flow is exactly min(exp(phi_i/T),exp(phi_j/T))/2, giving unique Gibbs weights for a single unit and a multinomial invariant count law for independent units. The top-k Gibbs masses strictly increase with inverse temperature for nonconstant depths. Vacancy is strictly Schur-convex. For sampled (rather than mean) Gini, conditioning a pair on its total occupancy gives a symmetric convex binomial Bernstein polynomial with strict midpoint curvature for at least two units, establishing strict Schur-convexity. Bounded quenched depths and \(M/L\to m\) give uniform binomial-to-Poisson approximation; a bounded-differences variance estimate proves empirical histogram convergence; a uniformly bounded Poisson intensity gives the stated Chernoff tail. Actual finite rational detailed balance and exact expectation tests passed from the standalone code. Edge conditions (equal depths, one unit, possible even-cycle period, fixed T) are explicitly distinguished.

evidence: Known detailed-balance and Gibbs facts yield \(p_i\propto\exp(\phi_i/T)\).

value.rationale: The cited 2026 model makes temperature-dependent Pareto fits and an intermediate-temperature inequality peak central to its interpretation. The result proves a substantive finite-particle strict inequality for the actual sampled Gini and vacant-site fraction, so an equilibrium peak is impossible under the paper's own specified micro-rule. It also identifies an explicit thermodynamic money distribution and a super-exponential tail bound, separating finite-range power-law fits from true equilibrium scaling. These are mathematically motivated structural conclusions with direct implications for interpreting the new model, beyond a normalization check. Limits and finite-time risks are stated.
